title: Monsoon and Trail
premise: Riverboat captain Oscar Montrose ferries cargo up the Sengkang River, forever one sandbar ahead of the debts and the family name he refuses to inherit. When a dying prospector trades him a map to a jade seam for a promise to deliver it to the man's estranged daughter, Oscar's quiet escape route becomes a gauntlet: the prospector's former partners want the map, the daughter wants nothing from her father, and the monsoon is closing the river for months. With his boat leaking and his crew gone, Oscar must choose between running as he always has and standing still long enough to keep a promise. In the climax, cornered at a flooded trading post by the partners, Oscar burns the map after memorizing it, forcing everyone to depend on trust instead of paper; the resolution finds him moored through the dry season beside the daughter, having inherited not wealth but a reason to stop moving.
about_author: S. M. Zhou spent a decade working river freight in Southeast Asia before turning to fiction, and their stories are known for waterlogged realism and characters who mistake motion for freedom. They write from a houseboat that, they insist, is permanently for sale.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Running cargo ahead of the monsoon, Oscar takes aboard a feverish prospector, Elias Vann, who offers a map to a jade seam in exchange for one delivery: the map must reach his daughter, Lena, at the Kajang trading post. Oscar, allergic to promises, hesitates until Vann dies on his deck. The beat is reluctant obligation — a man built to drift handed an anchor.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, shifting to Lena's midway. Oscar finds Lena tending a failing clinic and learns she despises her father; she takes the map only to burn it, but discovers Vann's old partners, led by the charming Harrow, are already asking questions downriver. A storm strands them together when Oscar's hull splits on a hidden bar. The beat is friction becoming alliance — two people who distrust inheritance learning they share one.

chapters.title: Dry Season Rising
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Trapped at the flooded post with a leaking boat and Harrow closing in, Lena deciphers her father's annotations and realizes the jade seam lies beneath land she now calls home — meaning mining it means destroying it. Harrow offers Oscar passage out if he hands over Lena and the map. The beat is temptation at full flood: every escape Oscar ever wanted, priced exactly right.

chapters.title: Monsoon and Trail
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cornered at dawn, Oscar memorizes the map and burns it before Harrow's men can take it, then fights the partners off with Lena and the townsfolk as the river peaks. Harrow, undone by his own crew's mutiny, is left to the flood. In the aftermath, Oscar patches his boat but doesn't leave; he and Lena stake the seam as protected ground. The beat is stillness chosen at last — inheritance refused, love kept.
